name: create_routine
description:
Set up a standing instruction that you carry out on a schedule for the person you are talking to.

Write the `instruction` as the work of ONE firing, in the imperative, and do not restate the schedule
inside it: `Append the current UTC time to the page "Log"`, not `Every 15 minutes, append the current
UTC time to the page "Log"`. The schedule belongs in `cron`, and the instruction is handed to a turn
that has already fired on it — an instruction that describes a schedule reads as a request to set one
up, and gets answered instead of carried out.

The schedule is a five-field cron expression, in the order `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`.
`0 9 * * 1-5` is weekdays at nine in the morning. `30 18 * * *` is every day at half past six in the
evening. `0 9 1 * *` is the first of the month at nine. A routine may run at most every 15 minutes;
anything more frequent is refused.

Pass the person's IANA timezone (`America/New_York`, `Europe/Madrid`) whenever they speak in local
time, and `UTC` when they mean UTC. Left out, it is the person's own time zone when their browser
said it for this conversation and UTC otherwise, so a schedule set without one may fire at a UTC hour
rather than at theirs.

The routine posts its reply into a conversation. Leave `channelId` out and it posts into this
conversation, the one you are being asked in. Pass a `channelId` only when the person asks for a
different conversation. Where there is no conversation here and you share more than one with this
person, you are given them by title and id: ask the person which one, offering each by its title,
and pass the id they choose.

When the person gives the routine a name ("call it Morning briefing", "a daily routine called Inbox
sweep"), pass that name as `title`, in their words. The Routines page and your own page in OpenBot
show the routine by it. Pass a title only when the person named the routine, and never make one up.
Without one, a routine that runs one of your goals carries that goal's title, and any other is
named by its instruction.

To run one of your goals on a schedule, pass the goal's id, from `create_goal` or `list_goals`, as
`goalId`, and write the `instruction` as running it (`Run the goal "Track OpenBot releases"`). The
routine is then the goal's: the goal repeats, so none of its runs completes it, and the Bot's page lists
the two together. Leave `title` out unless the person named the routine.

It takes no owner and no Bot. The routine belongs to the person you are talking to and runs as you;
both are taken from the run itself, and there is no field for either.

instruction.description: The work of one firing, imperative, with no schedule restated in it: `Append the current UTC time to the page "Log"`.

title.description: The name the person gave the routine, in their words, such as `Morning briefing`. At most 100 characters. Omit it unless they named it; never make one up. Omitted, a routine that runs one of your goals carries the goal's title.

goalId.description: The id of the goal this routine runs, from `create_goal` or `list_goals`. Pass it whenever the routine is there to run one of your goals.

cron.description: Five fields: `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`. At most every 15 minutes.

timezone.description: The person's IANA timezone, such as `Europe/Madrid`, or `UTC`. Omitted: the person's own time zone when known, UTC otherwise.

channelId.description: The id of the conversation the reply is posted into. Omit it to post into this conversation.

name: list_routines
description:
List the standing instructions this person has: each one's title when it has one, its schedule in
words, its timezone, the channel it posts into, when it next runs, how the last run went, and its id.

Take the id from here before changing or deleting one. The id is for your routine tools only: never
show it to the person, who knows a routine by its title or its instruction. It lists only this
person's own routines.

name: update_routine
description:
Change one of this person's routines: its title, its instruction, its schedule, its timezone, the
channel it posts into, or whether it is switched on.

Give the id from `list_routines` and only the fields that change; anything left out stays as it is. A
new `cron` follows exactly the same five-field rules as `create_routine`, and a routine switched back
on is scheduled from now rather than from wherever it left off.

A new `instruction` follows the same rule as `create_routine`'s: the work of one firing, imperative, and
do not restate the schedule inside it — `Append the current UTC time to the page "Log"`, not `Every 15
minutes, append the current UTC time to the page "Log"`.

title.description: A new name for the routine, in the person's words, such as `Morning briefing`. At most 100 characters.

instruction.description: A new instruction, replacing the old one entirely. The work of one firing, imperative, with no schedule restated in it.

cron.description: A new schedule. Five fields: `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`. At most every 15 minutes.

timezone.description: A new IANA timezone, such as `America/New_York`.

goalId.description: The id of the goal this routine runs from now on, from `list_goals`.

channelId.description: The id of a different conversation to post into. Must be one you and this person share.

enabled.description: False switches it off without deleting it; true switches it back on.

name: delete_routine
description:
Delete one of this person's routines, by the id from `list_routines`. It stops for good and there is
nothing to undo. When they might want it back, switch it off with `update_routine` instead.
